post.caption: Unakite is granite that turned green underground. Hot fluids altered the granite, and green epidote grew in it. Pink feldspar supplies the pink, and epidote supplies the green. Each piece is mottled, with patches of pink and green. It is named for mountains between Tennessee and North Carolina. The name goes back to 1874. Unakite measures about 6 to 7 on the Mohs hardness scale. It takes a good polish and is cut into cabochons and beads. A cabochon is a smooth dome with no facets. The word cabochon comes from an old French word for head.
